title: Stratified launch lanes and dependency oddities notebook
content:
Context & purpose:
This is a working notebook for the upcoming stratified launch (week of 2026-10-18). Goal: provide a compact, operator-friendly view of lanes, dependency oddities we've encountered in sims, and the minimum safety hedges we must have in place before traffic ramps. Not a formal runbook — think: a field notebook for the launch steward and the evening watch.

High-level approach (stratified lanes):
- Lane A (core customers, n=50): pinned model v2.3, dedicated pool. Target latency SLO: p95 < 200ms. Canary start: 10% traffic -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%.
- Lane B (internal + beta orgs): model v2.3-quant (CPU fallback enabled). aggressive batching allowed. Canary: 20% steady -> 60% (24h) -> 100%.
- Lane C (experimental variants + A/B features): model v2.4-experimental. Short-lived variants only; telemetry sampling at 100% diff sampling. Always behind a feature flag.
- Lane D (safety-lane): synthetic-only traffic, mirrors production prefixes; used for immediate rollback/fastfail.

Key dependency oddities observed in stress sims (summary):
1) KV cache eviction mismatch (serving-runtime): under long-prefix traffic, eviction triggered earlier than expected when burst concurrency > 1200 on A100 nodes. Effect: tail-latency spikes and occasional OOMs on pooled nodes. Repro path: RE-1248. Temporary hedge: smaller max-prefix-size per request for lane A until patch lands.
2) Canary-mesh route flaps when control-plane refresh (2s jitter) aligns with autoscaler cooldowns (60s). Symptom: short 502 blips on <1% of requests during scale-up. Mitigation: extend autoscaler cooldown to 90s for rollout window; enable request-level retries 2->3 with idempotency header for internal/beta lanes.
3) Tokenization regression in v2.4-experimental: a handful (~0.03%) of prompts produce tokenization mismatch (different byte-level routing) causing model mismatch and QA diffs. Not a crash, but impacts eval gating. Action: block v2.4 on lane C for customer-facing routes; run focused eval set per PR before enabling.
4) Region-specific infra drift: eu-west caches still on older CUDA driver (510) vs expected 520 in prod. Causes slower kernel selection and higher CPU fallback. Plan: schedule infra upgrade in maintenance window 2026-10-20 02:00-04:00 UTC; do not route region-critical customers until verified.

Minimum safety hedges (MUST HAVE before any traffic change):
- Telemetry sniffer active: p50/p95/p99 for latency, token-rate, errors per-second, OOMs. Dashboard URL pinned to watch channel.
- Canary sampling rule: deterministic sample mapping (customer ID hash -> canary cohort) to avoid double-flipping.
- Fast rollback toggle: one-click feature flag to pin traffic back to previous model + autoscaler reset. Owner: Asha.
- Quarantine lane: ability to divert 0.5% of traffic to Lane D for live forensic capture.
- Cost throttle: global per-model token-rps throttle to avoid runaway billing from malformed prompts.

Night-by-night rollout calendar (proposed compact view):
- Day -3 (2026-10-15): final preflight dryrun on staging; smoke harness: 1m synthetic sessions across lanes. Confirm no KV eviction under 30k prefix load.
- Day -2 (2026-10-16): telem & alert burn-in; create watch playlist; run internal beta cohort at 5% traffic.
- Day -1 (2026-10-17): freeze (no infra changes), train support on rollback procedure, pre-provision extra dedicated nodes for Lane A.
- Day 0 (2026-10-18): start lane A canary 10% -> monitor 3h -> 25% -> monitor 6h -> 50% -> 12h -> 100% (if no signals). Concurrent: lane B ramp to 20%.
- Day 1-3: slow steady ramp for lane B + 24h canary window for lane C experiments (but blocked for customer routes).
- Contingency window (2026-10-19 00:00 - 2026-10-20 08:00 UTC): reserved quiet hours for any rollback + infra upgrade verification in eu-west.

Smoke & acceptance checklist (quick pass before each ramp step):
- Telemetry green: error-rate < 0.05% vs baseline; p95 within +20% of baseline; OOMs = 0.
- Stability: autoscaler no more than 1 scale event per 15m per pool during first 6h.
- Token correctness: run 100 golden prompts, diff outputs to baseline; if >5 mismatches, hold.
- Cost sanity: token-rate-to-throughput ratio within expected band; abnormal spikes flagged.
- Customer helpline: CS standby and pre-crafted comms ready if any lane affected.

Failure modes & immediate actions (operator cheatsheet):
- Tail latency spike (p99 > target for 15m) -> reduce batch sizes on lane B, pin lane A to dedicated pool, increase KV cache headroom. Owner: Marcus.
- OOM on pool node -> disable pooling on affected pool, drain node, rollback recent scaling or model change, open incident channel #re-deploy.
- 5xx surge > threshold -> revert to previous model on affected routes, enable safety-lane diversion to D.
- Tokenization mismatch detection -> pause lane C, trigger targeted eval, notify research.

Communications plan (short scripts):
- Internal all-hands (ops): immediate pings on #release-ops and #infra-alerts with prefilled incident template.
- Customer-facing short note: for customers in lane A (if impacted more than 5% error-rate for >30m), send templated note: subject = "Service degradation affecting generative responses" with ETA and actions. Draft saved in linked artifacts. Owner: Priya.

Open questions / TODOs (work items to resolve before Day 0):
- [ ] RE-1248: confirm patch for KV eviction landed and validated in canary; if not, add request-level prefix cap per SDK. (owner: Asha)
- [ ] Autoscaler cooldown experiment: revert to 90s for rollout window and observe. (owner: Liam)
- [ ] eu-west CUDA upgrade scheduling confirmation + post-upgrade perf smoke. (owner: Sofia)
- [ ] Add tokenization quick-check to PR gate for v2.4 (owner: Research lead).
- [ ] Short walkthrough doc for CS describing lane differences and expected customer impact. (owner: Priya)

Quick checklist for the launch steward (to tape to console):
1) Confirm telemetry dashboards live and alerts routed.
2) Validate lane mapping and sampling deterministic hash seeded.
3) Pre-provision dedicated nodes for Lane A and mark out-of-service nodes for safety.
4) Confirm rollback toggle visible and tested in staging.
5) Ensure #release-ops watchers present for first 12h.

Field notes / informal observations (from rehearsal 2026-09-30):
- During a 4h soak sim, we saw autoscaler thrash when synthetic traffic had microbursts; increasing cooldown to 90s flattened the curve.
- Standalone CPU fallback pegged a maintenance host in eu-west; that host had older drivers. Upgrading that host dropped tail-latency by 18ms.
- The operator UX for the one-click rollback needs a confirmation modal listing active cohorts — low friction is good but too-easy rollback caused accidental flips during demo.

Appendix: quick links & artifacts
- JIRA RE-1248 (KV eviction).
- Canary analysis notebook (internal): /confluence/RE/canary-analysis-2026-09-30
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4021 (autoscaler tuning)

If you're reading this as the steward: keep this file open, annotate notes under "Field notes" as you go, call out any novel oddity to the linked JIRA immediately. This doc will be trimmed and converted into a formal runbook post-mortem — for now, use it as the single source-of-truth during the ramp window.

-- Marcus (launch steward)
